raw:
The gardens are quiet enough to make the Academy seem farther away than it is.

You follow the pale paths between low stone walls, where flowering vines have been trained into arches and the wind from the plateau arrives softened, carrying the mineral smell of the storm below. Lamp-globes wake gradually along the paths as the afternoon dims.

At one turn, you can see the western bridge through a gap in the hedges: hard light laid across open air, its far end swallowed by blue-grey cloud. At another, the shuttered windows of Garvey House catch the last of the daylight.

You pass no one close enough to require acknowledgment. Somewhere beyond the garden wall, a practice blade strikes another with a bright, regular ring; farther off, bells mark the hour.

By the time you return to the house-side path, the lamps burn steadily overhead and an hour has gone by.
